title: Google reports negative free cash flow amid AI spending spree
excerpt: Google made nearly $120 billion last quarter, but its escalating AI infrastructure costs pushed free cash flow into the red.
content_html:
Google made nearly $120 billion last quarter, but its escalating AI infrastructure costs pushed free cash flow into the red.

 

By

Olivia Tauber

Olivia Tauber

Deputy Digital Culture Editor

Olivia Tauber is the deputy editor of digital culture, covering creators, media, movies, beauty, and more. Based in New York, her work has appeared in The New York Times, Vanity Fair, The Cut, Teen Vogue, Complex, and Interview Magazine. She holds a Master's degree in Journalism from NYU and a Bachelor's from the University of Michigan. She also runs Fan Mail, a weekly pop-culture newsletter.

Read Full Bio

 

on July 24, 2026

Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on Flipboard

Credit: Cheng Xin/Getty Images

Google made nearly $120 billion in earnings last quarter. Somehow, that still was not enough to cover what the company is pouring into AI.

This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.

Alphabet, Google’s parent company, announced Wednesday, July 22, that it recorded negative free cash flow of $5.9 billion for the second quarter of 2026, marking the first time that figure has fallen below zero since the company went public. Google generated $39.1 billion in operating cash flow, but spent $44.9 billion on capital projects, with most of the money going toward the servers, data centers, and networking equipment needed to support its AI products.

This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.

To be clear, Google is still making plenty of money. In the Q2 2026 earnings report, the company disclosed $119.8 billion in quarterly revenue, a 24 percent increase from the same period last year. Its operating income reached $40.8 billion, while its net income climbed to a record $112.1 billion.

You May Also Like

There is an important catch to that record profit, however. Much of it came from Alphabet’s investments rather than its main businesses. The company reported approximately $98 billion in other, primarily from unrealized gains in its portfolio of equity investments. Those gains reflect assets that increased in value but were not necessarily sold for cash.

Free cash flow offers a look at the money Google actually had left after covering its operating expenses and investments in assets such as equipment and facilities. The company typically produces billions of dollars in free cash flow each quarter. This time, though, its rapidly growing infrastructure costs consumed more cash than its businesses generated.

And Google does not plan to slow down.

This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.

Also on July 22, the company raised its expected capital spending for 2026 to between $195 billion and $205 billion. Google had previously told investors during its first-quarter earnings report on April 29 that it expected to spend between $180 billion and $190 billion this year. The updated forecast would be more than twice the approximately $91 billion it spent in 2025.

Mashable Light Speed

The bill is expected to keep growing next year. During Alphabet’s call on Wednesday, Chief Financial Officer Anat Ashkenazi told investors that capital expenditures would increase "significantly" again in 2027.

"We expect that free cash flow will remain under pressure driven by our investments in technical infrastructure, which enable us to capitalize on the AI opportunity and continue to drive attractive returns," Ashkenazi said.

So, where is all that money going?

According to Ashkenazi, approximately 60 percent of Google’s technical infrastructure spending during the quarter went toward servers. The remaining 40 percent went toward data centers and networking equipment.

Google also said it needs that additional capacity to meet demand from outside cloud customers and support its own products, including Search, Gemini, and Google Workspace. There are already signs that some of the spending is paying off: Google reported that Cloud revenue reached $24.8 billion during the quarter, an 82 percent increase from the previous year, while its operating income more than tripled to $8.8 billion.

Google’s other major businesses continued to grow, too. The company also reported that Search advertising generated $63.3 billion, YouTube advertising brought in $11.1 billion, and revenue from subscriptions, platforms, and devices reached $12.9 billion. Google said demand for AI subscriptions helped boost its Google One business.

They are hardly the only company writing enormous checks for AI. Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and Meta are collectively expected to invest more than $700 billion this year, largely in data centers, chips, and electricity required to build and run their AI systems.

Investors, however, did not appear reassured by Google’s growth. Alphabet shares fell nearly 7 percent on Thursday, July 23, the day after the company raised its spending forecast and warned that free cash flow would remain under pressure.

This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.

Google still has a substantial financial cushion, but with the company already warning that infrastructure spending will climb significantly again in 2027, this may not be the last quarter in which Google’s enormous AI bill outpaces the cash coming in.

谷歌上季度盈利近 1200 亿美元，但其不断上升的人工智能基础设施成本导致自由现金流出现赤字。

 

By

奥利维亚·陶伯

奥利维亚·陶伯

数字文化副编辑

Olivia Tauber 是《数字文化》副主编，内容涵盖创作者、媒体、电影、美妆等。 她居住在纽约，作品曾出现在《纽约时报》、《名利场》、《The Cut》、《Teen Vogue》、《Complex》和《Interview》杂志上。 她拥有纽约大学新闻学硕士学位和密歇根大学学士学位。 她还经营《粉丝邮报》（Fan Mail），这是一份每周流行文化时事通讯。

谷歌上季度盈利近 1200 亿美元。 不知何故，这仍然不足以涵盖该公司在人工智能领域的投入。

此推文当前不可用。 它可能正在加载或已被删除。

谷歌母公司 Alphabet 于 7 月 22 日星期三宣布，2026 年第二季度自由现金流为负 59 亿美元，这是该公司上市以来该数字首次降至零以下。 谷歌产生了 391 亿美元的运营现金流，但在资本项目上花费了 449 亿美元，其中大部分资金用于支持其人工智能产品所需的服务器、数据中心和网络设备。

此推文当前不可用。 它可能正在加载或已被删除。

需要明确的是，谷歌仍然赚了很多钱。 在2026年第二季度财报中，该公司披露季度营收1198亿美元，较去年同期增长24%。 其营业收入达到408亿美元，净利润攀升至创纪录的1121亿美元。

你可能也喜欢

然而，创纪录的利润有一个重要的问题。 其中大部分来自 Alphabet 的投资，而不是其主营业务。 该公司公布的其他资金约为 980 亿美元，主要来自其股权投资组合的未实现收益。 这些收益反映了价值增加但不一定出售现金的资产。

自由现金流可以让我们了解谷歌在支付运营费用以及设备和设施等资产投资后实际剩下的资金。 该公司通常每个季度产生数十亿美元的自由现金流。 然而，这一次，其快速增长的基础设施成本消耗的现金比其业务产生的现金还要多。

谷歌并不打算放慢脚步。

此推文当前不可用。 它可能正在加载或已被删除。

同样在 7 月 22 日，该公司将 2026 年预期资本支出上调至 1950 亿美元至 2050 亿美元之间。 谷歌此前曾在4月29日的第一季度财报中告诉投资者，预计今年的支出将在1800亿至1900亿美元之间。 更新后的预测将是 2025 年支出约 910 亿美元的两倍多。

可混搭光速

预计该法案明年将继续增长。 在周三的 Alphabet 电话会议上，首席财务官阿纳特·阿什肯纳齐 (Anat Ashkenazi) 告诉投资者，2027 年资本支出将再次“大幅”增加。

阿什肯纳齐表示：“我们预计，由于我们对技术基础设施的投资，自由现金流将继续面临压力，这使我们能够利用人工智能机会并继续带来有吸引力的回报。”

那么，这些钱都去哪儿了？

Ashkenazi 表示，本季度 Google 大约 60% 的技术基础设施支出用于服务器。 剩下的 40% 用于数据中心和网络设备。

谷歌还表示，它需要额外的容量来满足外部云客户的需求并支持自己的产品，包括搜索、Gemini 和 Google Workspace。 已有迹象表明部分支出正在获得回报：谷歌报告称，本季度云收入达到 248 亿美元，比上年增长 82%，而其营业收入则增长两倍多，达到 88 亿美元。

谷歌的其他主要业务也持续增长。 该公司还报告称，搜索广告收入为 633 亿美元，YouTube 广告收入为 111 亿美元，来自订阅、平台和设备的收入达到 129 亿美元。 谷歌表示，对人工智能订阅的需求有助于推动其 Google One 业务。

他们并不是唯一一家为人工智能开出巨额支票的公司。 谷歌、亚马逊、微软和 Meta 今年预计将投资超过 7000 亿美元，主要用于构建和运行人工智能系统所需的数据中心、芯片和电力。

然而，投资者似乎并没有对谷歌的增长感到放心。 7 月 23 日星期四，Alphabet 股价下跌近 7%，此前该公司上调支出预测并警告自由现金流将继续面临压力。

谷歌仍然拥有大量的财务缓冲，但该公司已经警告称，基础设施支出将在 2027 年再次大幅攀升，这可能不是谷歌巨额人工智能支出超过现金收入的最后一个季度。
